{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMdNDs8AAAABbFfAVg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnXy5zhEqmrc", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnXy5", "number": 65, "title": "Add body-moving official VMD motions to Uka and Gene synchronized comparison (IK/physics off)", "body": "## Problem

Issue #63 delivered one synchronized public VMD expression sample per character, but the selected `04_littlesmile.vmd` (Uka) and `01_happy.vmd` (Gene) have skeletal keys only at frame 0. Their visible time-dependent animation is primarily facial morphs. The next demo should **visibly move the body/arms/upper body over time** while preserving the MMD (direct PMX) vs glTF side-by-side comparison.

**Scope and ownership:** This Issue is the task specification for the designated implementer. No code changes, branches or PRs are to be created by the issue author. Keep **IK, physics and append/grant execution disabled** on both sides; this is not a request to implement those solvers.

## Expected outcome

Extend the current public Motion selector for **both Uka and Gene Light** with the official `02_laugh.vmd` and `22_apology.vmd` (or a demonstrably more suitable pinned official alternative if binding/visibility auditing reveals a blocker). Keep the existing Rest/manual and expression samples. The selected body-motion clips play with one shared absolute clock, and **both independently rendered panes** display meaningful, changing skeletal poses as well as any supported facial morphs.

## Verified source evidence

Pinned upstream repositories (already used by the project):
- [Uka motion/ at 659f0d1](https://github.com/mmdagent-ex/uka/tree/659f0d1a740fec68bb2817dc9c694a35e7a15f12/motion)
- [Gene motion/ at c7eace4](https://github.com/mmdagent-ex/gene/tree/c7eace43dffaccff6ad0597433ef85fa57c91e03/motion)

Independent direct inspection of VMD binary bone frame records (not visual confirmation) found:

| VMD | Bone records | Bone keys after frame 0 | Distinct bone tracks whose transforms change over time | Maximum bone frame |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Uka and Gene `02_laugh.vmd` (byte-identical) | 548 | 324 | 50 | 300 |
| Uka `22_apology.vmd` | 549 | 247 | 48 | 300 |
| Gene `22_apology.vmd` | 718 | 494 | 63 | 300 |
| Uka and Gene `stand.vmd` | 470 | 246 | 4 | 120 |
| Uka and Gene `33_angry.vmd` | 828 | 604 | 0 | 100 |

These figures count VMD key records and transform variation, **not successful binding to each PMX nor rendered body motion**. Do not infer visibility from record counts alone. The selected first candidate should be **02_laugh**, then **22_apology**. Both source repositories license their files under CC BY 4.0 with required credits; Gene additionally retains trademark/design restrictions described in its README.

Current [public-motion.md](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/public-motion.md) and [Issue #63](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/issues/63) describe the existing synchronized clock, asset audit, strict name-binding policy, morph preview, UI, rights and browser checks.

## Implementation steps

### Asset and track auditing
- [ ] From the pinned upstream commits, verify sizes/SHA-256 and binding coverage for **each model + each proposed VMD**, including unique/terminated exact PMX bone names, nonzero changing pose transforms, rejected/unmatched tracks, and active morph types. Review the existing [motion audit tool](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/tools/audit-public-motions.ts) and [public-motion audit data](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/public-motion-audit.json). Pick clips based on *actual bound, visible body motion* (arms/upper body/torso), not just frame counts.
- [ ] Preserve original binary bytes and model-specific attribution, notices and usage policies. Add chosen VMDs to both pinned allowlists `tools/uka-manifest.json` and `tools/gene-light-manifest.json`. Since `02_laugh` is byte-identical across upstream repositories, do not present it as a different file or uniquely Uka-authored asset. `22_apology` differs; use each model's own version.
- [ ] Apply conservative explicit name-binding rules. Unsupported material/group/bone/UV morphs and ambiguous records must be disclosed; do not silently treat them as executed. If a candidate activates unsupported morph families that cannot be isolated without distorting results, choose another officially licensed body-motion VMD or explicitly document the limitation and preserve source.

### Conversion and public playback
- [ ] Update `tools/public-motion.ts`, `tools/prepare-uka.ts` and `tools/prepare-example.ts` to produce *motion-specific* skinned BDEF conversion/transport artifacts with exact VMD retention, while sharing/avoiding needless duplication of source images and static geometry where practical. Do not break the current downloadable character glTF or overwrite its original animated asset without an intentional migration.
- [ ] Extend `examples/index.html` Motion selector and `examples/main.ts` state/loading to choose `Rest / manual`, the already available facial sample, `02_laugh`, and `22_apology` for the current character. Use concise recognizable labels. Keep the two pane headings **MMD** and **glTF**, no verbose introduction, current synchronized camera and mobile layout.
- [ ] The left side should evaluate VMD on direct PMX using its existing `MMDLoader` and a raw `AnimationMixer`; the right side should use `MMDVMDPlugin`/exact retained `VMDPlayer` without double-running core fallback animation. Both sides must use the **same selected VMD and single absolute timeline** (frame/30 seconds) for seek, pause, play, restart, loop. Changing motions/models disposes or releases old actions/players and restores the correct base pose.
- [ ] Keep **IK, grant/append, physics, Bullet/Ammo and other unsupported deformation execution OFF**, as in #63. A bone animation should actually move the body using authored keys, not simulate missing IK. Avoid cross-engine differences from applying different subsets of VMD records.
- [ ] The current `examples/motion-preview.ts` optimizes GPU morph buffers to five motion-relevant targets. Recompute projection safely **per motion** without silently losing animated vertex targets; do not upload every Uka morph target unnecessarily or rewrite source names. Verify full CPU/retained identity and resource cleanup, including Toon/PBR instances.
- [ ] Retain verified rights, source attribution, unchanged binary files, caveats in collapsed About & credits and concise per-motion diagnostic/binding summaries. Record which clips provide authored body animation and which features are deliberately omitted.

### Tests and acceptance
- [ ] Both public characters can select and play **at least two** additional visible body-motion clips, preferably the official `02_laugh` and `22_apology`, in addition to existing Rest and facial sample.
- [ ] For each model, test at least two distinct non-zero VMD times that yield visibly different **bone-driven rendered geometry** on **both** panes. Assert bone local/world transform differences against the rest pose (not just morph weights or a clock changing), and compare left/right poses with clear tolerances if coordinate conventions permit.
- [ ] Test pause freeze, arbitrary seek (including backwards), restart determinism, looping, motion/model switching, source binding errors, corrupted/missing file retry, and desktop/mobile control layout. Confirm both views share the exact same VMD time and no IK/physics/Ammo initializes.
- [ ] Maintain existing Uka/Gene expression sample, material Toon/PBR, Outline, synchronized camera, load/error handling, credits, internal synthetic harness and tests.
- [ ] Run `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, targeted real-asset Playwright browser suites, `npm run check:links`, and `git diff --check`; report actual results/skips and avoid unsupported claims of original MikuMikuDance parity.

## Optional validation

Visually inspect and capture desktop/mobile playback of `02_laugh` and `22_apology` on both characters, focusing on arms/upper body. A future issue can add walking/dance motions or IK/physics comparison, but that is deliberately out of scope.

## Required post-merge verification

None required, unless the implementer changes the deployment requirements explicitly.
